source: Eaton, PXM 1000 User Manual MN150009EN (June 2021), chapter 6 Communication
notes: Modbus RTU on the RS-485 port: function 03 (read), 10 hex (write), 01 and 05 (relays), 02 (digital inputs). Factory defaults from the manual: address 1, 19200 baud, no parity (setting NON1), 8 data bits; the parity registers 0FFFH and 1030H take 0 = even, 1 = odd, 2 = none with two stop bits, 3 = none with one stop bit.
Addresses are the hexadecimal data addresses of the manual, sent as they are (address base 0). The relays (coils) and digital inputs (discrete inputs) have their own address spaces from 0000H.
32-bit integers have the high word first, as the manual states; the 32-bit floats are sent high word first as in its example (50.00 Hz = 42480000H). Bytes are big-endian.

The float registers 4000H to 4047H and 3000H to 303BH are secondary values unless the meter is set to primary mode (Basic Parameter Mode, 101DH): multiply voltage by PT1/PT2, current by CT1/CT2 and power by both, as the relationship in each description says. The meter holds PT1 (1005H), PT2 (1007H), CT1 (1008H) and CT2 (1009H) for this. CT2 is taken as 1 for voltage-type, Rogowski and mA sensors (manual, chapter 6.3).

Integer values use the scale of Table 46 where it is fixed (for example frequency /100, power factor /1000, THD and harmonics /10000 as a percentage, phase angle /10, current /1000 in secondary mode); the voltage and power integers also need the PT and CT ratios. Energy (Dword) is /10 in primary mode and /1000 in secondary mode; the scale shown is the primary one (default).

The MIN block (41E5H to 4293H) is given in the manual only by its range and the statement that it has the same format as the MAX block; it is laid out here on that basis. The time stamp fields of the MIN/MAX, alarm and SOE blocks are listed as one register per field (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond).

Left out: the alarm setting tables (50 to 52), the I/O module and analog-output settings (53 to 61), data logging (78 to 82) and time-of-use settings, which are configuration blocks rather than readings. Reserved addresses are skipped.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
